Warehouse Targets NZ$100M Operating Profit in 3-5 Years, Revises Dividend Policy
By David Winning

SYDNEY--New Zealand-based retailer Warehouse Group has set a goal of more than quadrupling operating profit within three to five years, while revising its dividend policy and signaling it could resume payouts this fiscal year.

Warehouse said it is targeting an operating profit of 100 million New Zealand dollars, equivalent to US$56.3 million, in three to five years. If achieved, that would represent a significant jump on the NZ$22.6 million reported for the 2026 fiscal year.

Chief Executive Mark Stirton said the strategy didn't rely on any single initiative. Warehouse aims to open four to five stores annually across its three brands, and intends to simplify its supply chain.
"We will first improve our existing business, then regain market share while pursuing growth through new stores and new profit streams," Stirton said.
Warehouse said it has revised its dividend policy to target a payout ratio of 50-70% of adjusted net profit. Directors intend to consider resuming dividends for the 2027 fiscal year.

Monday's strategy update also included a snapshot of first-quarter trading. Warehouse said group sales are broadly in line with a year ago and its margin was stronger than 12 months earlier, despite a subdued retail climate.
